I farm wheat and maize on the same 12 mu in rotation, so I will use the full 12 mu for winter wheat first and then the same 12 mu for summer maize after wheat harvest. I have 40 years of experience, good education, and well irrigation, so I will run a fairly intensive but controlled system. I do not need to be conservative with seed choice, so I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed to keep yield stable. Because my land is not large, I can manage timing carefully and keep inputs precise instead of spreading risk across many fields.

For winter wheat, I will keep fertilizer at a medium-high level because irrigated wheat in southern Hebei responds well when nutrition is not limiting. I will irrigate three times if water conditions stay normal: once for overwintering or before freeze if needed, once at jointing, and once around grain filling. I will use rotary tillage after maize residue management because it is efficient on my scale and fits the wheat-maize system. I will plan a few pesticide applications, mainly because I do not want weeds, aphids, or disease pressure to cut yield on a small farm where every mu matters.

For summer maize, I will plant quickly after wheat harvest to protect the growing period. I will use hybrid seed because that is the most practical choice for yield and stand uniformity. I will apply more nitrogen to maize than to wheat, keep phosphorus moderate, and add potassium to support stalk strength and grain filling. With well irrigation, I will plan two irrigations, mainly around the big water demand stages if rainfall is not enough. I will keep pesticide use moderate and rely on timely field management more than excessive spraying. My goal is steady production, not gambling on either very low-input or overly aggressive input use.
